subject: Coord: US/EU DST mismatch — split-demo proposal & calendar anchors
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moreno <elena@finbridge.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Coord: US/EU DST mismatch — split-demo proposal & calendar anchors

Hi Elena —

Quick heads-up: we noticed the upcoming DST change creates a one-week offset between the US and EU clocks (EU moves back earlier than the US this year). That affects the demo windows we discussed and will make a single all-region slot tricky for some of your participants.

Options we propose (all times given with common conversions):

1) Single session with a short core overlap (recommended)
   - Core overlap: 15:00 UTC / 08:00 PT / 16:00 CET (40 min shared demo, then 20–30 min breakouts)
   - Pros: everyone sees the main flow live; consistent Q&A.
   - Cons: APAC will be early/late depending on region.

2) Split demo (staggered): EU/APAC session + US session the next business day
   - EU/APAC: 14:00–15:00 CET (13:00–14:00 UTC)
   - US follow-up: 16:00–17:00 PT (00:00–01:00 UTC next day)
   - Pros: more localized times per region; smaller live groups for deeper questions.

3) Recording + abbreviated live Q&A for each region
   - Pre-record main demo; host a 30-min regional Q&A on chosen local time.

Proposed concrete anchors we can calendar-in immediately (pick one):
- Tue, 2 Nov 2026 — Core overlap: 15:00 UTC (08:00 PT / 16:00 CET)
- Wed, 3 Nov 2026 — Split: EU session 14:00 CET; US session next-day 16:00 PT
- Fri, 5 Nov 2026 — Recording + regional Q&As (EU 15:00 CET, US 08:00 PT)

Attached: demo-deck-v2.pdf and a draft mutual-action-plan.xlsx with suggested owners for follow-ups.

Ask: can you confirm preferred anchor and who from FinBridge will join each segment (names + roles)? If none of the times work, tell me the tightest window you have and we’ll adapt (we can also run a short recorded core and live deep-dive).

Thanks — I’ll hold tentative calendar slots until we lock this.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake | Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Elena Moreno <elena@finbridge.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@finbridge.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 16:22:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Coord: US/EU DST mismatch — split-demo proposal & calendar anchors

Thanks Jordan — really appreciate the options. Quick notes from my side:

- Preferred: Split demo (option 2). We have a big EU contingent and a smaller US engineering team that prefers an off-peak follow-up.
- Proposed EU slot: Wed, 3 Nov 2026, 14:00–15:00 CET (Lucia, our infra lead, will join).
- Proposed US slot: Thu, 4 Nov 2026, 16:00–17:00 PT (we can do a short recap + live Q&A for the US team).

Two asks: 1) can you confirm who will run the EU session and who will host the US follow-up? 2) We’d like access to a trial tenant beforehand (read-only) — can that be arranged and shared securely?

If you can send calendar invites with explicit time-zone conversions (we had confusion last time), that’d be great.

Best,
Elena
Elena Moreno | Head of Platform Integrations
FinBridge Solutions
elena@finbridge.com | +44 20 7946 02 11

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Elena Moreno <elena@finbridge.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Coord: US/EU DST mismatch — split-demo proposal & calendar anchors

Elena — great, split demo sounds like the cleanest path. Quick answers:

- EU session lead: Hannah Schmitt (I’ll have Hannah run the product demo and architecture Q&A).
- US follow-up host: Vivek Kulkarni (will handle the hands-on engineering questions and the integration checklist).

We can provide a read-only trial tenant and a short onboarding guide. I’ll loop in our solutions engineer to provision access and will share credentials via your SSO contact or an expiring link.

Next steps (I’ll action these by EOD):
- Hold provisional calendar invites for 3 Nov (EU) and 4 Nov (US) with explicit TZ conversions.
- Attach the trial tenant onboarding link + a short pre-demo checklist.
- Update the mutual action plan with owners (Hannah: EU demo; Vivek: US follow-up).

Hannah / Vivek — can you confirm you’re available for those anchors and whether you need any prep outputs from me (runbooks, deep-dive slides)?

Thanks — Jordan

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Moreno <elena@finbridge.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Coord: US/EU DST mismatch — split-demo proposal & calendar anchors

Jordan / Vivek — confirmed. I’ll lead the EU session on Wed 3 Nov (14:00–15:00 CET). Vivek, can you confirm Thu 4 Nov (16:00–17:00 PT) for the US follow-up?

Prep notes for the team:
- EU session: 35-minute demo (product + infra), 25-minute breakout for Lucía’s integration questions. I’ll include the new quantization/cost slide you added to deck-v2.
- US session: Vivek to cover API integration, rate limiting patterns, and a short live debugging demo.
- Calendar invites: please set them as separate events but link them in the description ("Part 1 / Part 2 — FinBridge") and include local time conversions (explicit HH:MM TZ). Add the MUTUAL ACTION PLAN link in both invites.

I’ll upload a small set of region-specific slides and a short runbook for the trial tenant into the shared Drive folder referenced in your email.

— Hannah

hannah.schmitt@redwood.com

Thanks everyone — that plan works for us. Confirming attendees:
- EU session (3 Nov): Elena Moreno (Head of Platform Integrations), Lucía Gomez (Infra Lead), Marco Silva (Security)
- US session (4 Nov): Tom Reed (Eng Manager - US), Priya Shah (Senior Dev)

We’ll need the trial tenant link by Monday morning (1 Nov CET) so Lucía can validate network egress rules. Also please add a short note in the invite about the DST interplay so our calendar auto-conversions don’t confuse folks — we had a bad mismatch last year.

If you want, I can share a calendar file (.ics) for each region that pins the local time and avoids client-side TZ issues.

Looking forward to it — Elena
